query: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloys are promising bond-coat candidates because of their mechanical properties and elevated-temperature oxidation resistance. Earlier HVAF-M3 work identified 15–45 μm feedstock as optimal for high-quality coatings, but applying the same composition and size range with the HVAF-i7 torch yielded acceptable coating quality yet inadequate thickness. Separate studies of conventional MCrAlY bond coats using the M3 system reported a slight gain in deposition efficiency at higher particle velocity and nozzle-specific best spray distances of 300 and 350 mm. The design target is a sufficiently thick, adherent bond coat that retains coating integrity, minimal as-sprayed oxidation, and durability during high-temperature thermal-barrier service, including deposition within internal diameters as small as 120 mm. What single intervention could overcome the thickness limitation? State the hypothesized intervention and mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline, define the deposition and service conditions under which it should remain effective, identify supporting evidence from the cited prior studies, and propose a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Increasing the particle velocity during the HVAF-i7 deposition process for FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy bond coats will enhance deposition efficiency, leading to thicker and well-adherent coatings with minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
generation.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy feedstock with a size distribution of 15–45 μm.
generation.intervention: Increase particle velocity during the HVAF-i7 deposition process.
generation.conditions: Deposition on substrates with internal diameters as small as 120 mm using spray distances around 300–350 mm under high-temperature thermal-barrier service conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: Greater kinetic energy of the particles enhances impact energy, promoting improved bonding and consolidating more material on the substrate.
generation.mechanism: Higher particle velocity increases the particles’ impact energy during deposition, which enhances the bonding efficiency and facilitates thicker coating build-up without significantly increasing as-sprayed oxidation.
generation.predicted_outcome: A significantly thicker bond coat than that obtained using standard HVAF-i7 settings, while maintaining coating adhesion and minimal oxidation compared to the baseline deposition using 15–45 μm feedstock.
generation.baseline: Coatings produced using standard HVAF-i7 parameters with 15–45 μm feedstock, which yield acceptable quality but insufficient thickness.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis is expected to hold for HVAF-i7 deposition with the specified feedstock size, nozzle spray distances around 300–350 mm, and for substrates with internal diameters down to 120 mm under high-temperature service conditions.
generation.uncertainty: The precise magnitude of the coating thickness improvement is uncertain until experimentally determined.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform a controlled deposition experiment using the HVAF-i7 process. Prepare two sets of samples under identical conditions (same substrate geometry, spray distance of 300–350 mm, and temperature conditions) with one set using the standard particle velocity and the other with an increased particle velocity.
measurements: Coating thickness measured via cross-sectional analysis
As-sprayed oxidation levels (using appropriate spectroscopic or diffraction techniques)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the samples produced with increased particle velocity do not exhibit a statistically significant increase in coating thickness—without detrimental changes in adhesion or oxidation levels—compared to the baseline samples produced with standard velocity, then the hypothesis is falsified.

drafts.hypothesis: Increasing the particle velocity during the HVAF-i7 process will improve deposition efficiency and achieve the required coating thickness for FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy bond coats without compromising coating integrity.
drafts.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy powder with a feedstock size of 15–45 μm.
drafts.intervention: Adjust the HVAF-i7 torch parameters to increase particle velocity, targeting spray distances around 300–350 mm.
drafts.conditions: Deposition on substrates with internal diameters as small as 120 mm under conditions that mimic high-temperature thermal-barrier service; maintaining minimized as-sprayed oxidation.
drafts.structural_mediator: Enhanced kinetic energy transfer on particle impact via higher particle velocity.
drafts.mechanism: Higher particle velocity provides increased kinetic energy that promotes stronger particle impaction and consolidation upon substrate contact. This improved particle bonding leads to thicker coatings and better adherence, without substantially enhancing oxidation during spraying.
drafts.predicted_outcome: A measurable increase in bond coat thickness while retaining the mechanical integrity and minimal oxidation levels compared to the baseline of using the standard HVAF-i7 parameters with 15–45 μm feedstock.
drafts.baseline: Coatings produced using the standard HVAF-i7 settings with 15–45 μm feedstock, which yield acceptable quality but insufficient thickness.
drafts.boundary: Effectiveness expected under spray distances near 300–350 mm and in deposition conditions targeting complex geometries (internal diameters down to 120 mm) that will also face high-temperature thermal-barrier service.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct a controlled experiment using the HVAF-i7 process where one set of samples is deposited with the standard particle velocity and another set is deposited with an increased particle velocity, while keeping other parameters constant. Ensure deposition at spray distances of approximately 300–350 mm on substrates with internal diameters of 120 mm. Subject the coated samples to identical high-temperature service simulations.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the increased particle velocity does not result in a statistically significant increase in coating thickness and/or results in degraded coating integrity (e.g., reduced adhesion or increased oxidation levels) compared to the baseline, then the hypothesis is falsified.

drafts.hypothesis: Using an extended-length nozzle with the HVAF-i7 torch to increase particle velocity and dwell time will yield thicker FeCoNiCrAl bond coats from 15–45 μm feedstock while maintaining low oxidation and strong adhesion.
drafts.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy feedstock in the 15–45 μm size range, stored and handled in standard inert conditions prior to spraying.
drafts.intervention: Replace the standard HVAF-i7 nozzle with a longer, optimized nozzle design to achieve higher particle velocity and enhanced deposition efficiency for thick bond coat formation.
drafts.conditions: HVAF-i7 spraying on steel or superalloy substrates, with standoff distances of 300–350 mm, using typical bond-coat spray parameters for elevated-temperature applications (e.g., TBC systems) and internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
drafts.structural_mediator: The extended nozzle geometry increases acceleration length for in-flight particles, improving strike energy and deposit build-up on the substrate surface.
drafts.mechanism: Prolonged and higher-velocity particle trajectories in the HVAF gas stream promote improved adherence and reduced rebound while controlling in-flight oxidation.
drafts.predicted_outcome: Relative to using a standard i7 nozzle, the extended nozzle configuration will produce at least 10–20% thicker coatings in the same number of passes, with comparable or reduced as-sprayed oxidation and adequate bond strength.
drafts.baseline: The baseline condition is the insufficient coating thickness obtained with the standard HVAF-i7 nozzle spraying 15–45 μm powder at 300–350 mm standoff distances.
drafts.boundary: This effect is expected to hold for 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl powder under typical HVAF bond-coat conditions and internal diameters ≥120 mm. Deviations in powder size or extreme geometries require further verification.

falsification_experiment.design: Use two sets of test coupons sprayed with 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl feedstock in an HVAF-i7 torch: one with the current standard nozzle (control) and another with the extended nozzle (treatment), holding all other parameters constant. Evaluate coatings deposited under identical torch power, feed rate, and standoff distances (300–350 mm).
measurements: Deposition efficiency (mass gain on coupons vs. feedstock used)
Bond strength (per ASTM C633 or equivalent)
Oxide content using XRD or EDS on cross-sections
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the extended-nozzle condition does not result in at least a 10–20% increase in average coating thickness, or if bond strength is significantly reduced, the hypothesis is falsified.

drafts.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy feedstock particles with a size range of 15–45 μm.
drafts.intervention: Adjust the feedstock particle size range to 25–35 μm for HVAF-i7 torch spraying.
drafts.conditions: HVAF-i7 torch spraying at nozzle-specific optimal spray distance (e.g., 300–350 mm) and internal diameters as small as 120 mm, targeting bond coat deposition for high-temperature thermal-barrier service.
drafts.structural_mediator: Particle velocity and deposition efficiency influenced by feedstock size distribution.
drafts.mechanism: A narrower particle size range (25–35 μm) optimizes particle velocity and thermal energy transfer during spraying, leading to improved deposition efficiency and coating thickness without compromising coating quality or oxidation resistance.
drafts.predicted_outcome: Compared to the 15–45 μm feedstock baseline, the 25–35 μm feedstock will result in a thicker bond coat with acceptable coating quality, minimal as-sprayed oxidation, and durability during high-temperature service.
drafts.baseline: HVAF-i7 torch spraying with 15–45 μm feedstock, yielding acceptable coating quality but inadequate thickness.
drafts.boundary: Effectiveness of the intervention is limited to HVAF-i7 torch spraying within nozzle-specific optimal spray distances and internal diameters as small as 120 mm.

falsification_experiment.design: Spray FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy coatings using the HVAF-i7 torch with feedstock particle size ranges of 15–45 μm and 25–35 μm. Measure coating thickness, quality, and oxidation resistance under identical deposition conditions (e.g., spray distance, internal diameter).
measurements: Adherence and integrity of the coating
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the 25–35 μm feedstock does not result in a thicker bond coat or compromises coating quality, oxidation resistance, or durability compared to the 15–45 μm baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
